Q1: p-Cresol exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) based on the Globally Harmonized System for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR), acute and chronic environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). Additionally, it shows potential hazards (Tier 2) for endocrine disruption (EDC) and inhalation hazards (IHL), drawing from a broader scientific perspective beyond GHS.
Q2: p-Cresol is recognized on several 'Lists of Concern,' including the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor. It is also regulated under the Clean Water Act and designated as a Hazardous Air Pollutant by the EPA.
Q3: p-Cresol is extensively characterized, indicated by its precise molecular formula (C7H8O) and classification as a 'Small Molecule,' rather than an ill-defined substance. With 35,000 scientific references and no data deficient (Tier 4) hazard categories, its hazard profile is considered comprehensive.
